Thought: I have the necessary information to calculate the surface energy. The surface area can be calculated using the x and y dimensions of the slab. The number of formula units in the bulk can be determined from the number of atoms in the bulk structure. I will now calculate the surface energy using the formula:

\[
\gamma = \frac{E_{\text{slab}} - N \cdot E_{\text{bulk}}}{2A}
\]

where:
- \( E_{\text{slab}} \) is the total energy of the slab.
- \( E_{\text{bulk}} \) is the total energy of the bulk per formula unit.
- \( N \) is the number of formula units in the slab.
- \( A \) is the surface area of the slab.
- The factor of 2 accounts for the two surfaces of the slab.

Given:
- Bulk energy: \(-7509.6216342278 \, \text{eV}\)
- Slab energy: \(-7286.67630708949 \, \text{eV}\)
- Number of atoms in bulk: 1125
- Number of atoms in slab: 1125
- Surface area: \(24.58279 \times 21.28932 \, \text{Å}^2\)

Action: Calculate the surface energy.
